message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may hold a maximum of **one month’s rent** (or two if the lease is for a month‑to‑month tenancy).
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• Repairs must be made within a reasonable time after notice. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or certified mail) of needed repairs.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or seek a court order. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report any harassment or unlawful entry. | | **Entry by Landlord** | • Landlord must give **at least 24 hours’ written notice** (unless it’s an emergency).
• Entry is allowed for repairs, inspections, or to show the unit to prospective tenants/buyers. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Rent Increases** | • For month‑to‑month leases, the landlord can raise rent **once per year** and must give **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, rent can only change if the lease itself is amended. | • Review your lease for any rent‑increase clauses. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Fixed‑term lease**: Must be honored unless both parties agree to terminate or the landlord breaches the lease.
• **Month‑to‑month lease**: Either party can terminate with **30 days’ written notice**. | • Provide written notice and keep a copy. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) if you suspect discrimination. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may **deduct the cost of repairs** from your rent (up to the amount of the rent). | • Keep receipts and provide the landlord with a written notice of the deduction. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **written notice** (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violations, 60 days for no‑cause termination of month‑to‑month).
• Eviction must go through the court; the landlord cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond to notices promptly; consider seeking legal counsel if you receive an eviction notice. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice, except in emergencies. | • Keep a record of any unauthorized entries. | | **Maintenance of Records** | • Landlord must keep records of rent payments and maintenance requests. | • Request copies if needed. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal aid for tenants (e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar associations). | • Contact a tenant advocacy group or legal aid office. | #### Quick Tips 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, rent receipts, repair requests, and any correspondence with the landlord. 2. **Know the Timeline** – Most notices (rent increase, entry, eviction) require a minimum of 24–30 days’ written notice. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Email or certified mail provides proof of delivery. 4. **Seek Mediation** – Many cities offer mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes before going to court. 5. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some Texas cities have additional tenant protections (e.g., rent control, eviction moratoriums). If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a repair, a notice of eviction, or a potential discrimination claim), let me know and I can give more tailored advice or help draft a letter.
